after.description: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS — Enable real-time preview of content edits made in Contentstack CMS, so that content authors see their changes reflected in the application without requiring a page refresh or republish.
after.title: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS

notes: Openspec provided empty acceptance criteria, so I authored the full list from the story description and file paths. Key design decisions: (1) AC-4 and AC-7 ensure zero regression for the 236 existing useContent callers when live preview is off — this is critical given the hook's centrality. (2) AC-5 and AC-6 cover error/resilience paths (connection loss, malformed payloads) that are likely in a real-time WebSocket-style system. (3) AC-9 addresses injection risk — preview payloads come from the CMS but could contain user-entered HTML, so sanitization parity with published content is essential. (4) AC-10 adds accessibility for live-updating regions. (5) AC-11 ensures type-contract stability so downstream consumers aren't broken by a different shape from preview vs. published. (6) AC-12 and AC-13 cover multi-session and navigation edge cases. (7) AC-14 addresses SSR/hydration safety inferred from the React component paths. CAVEAT: I do not have the file contents — my criteria assume useContent.ts is the integration point and contentstack.ts is the service layer. If the actual architecture differs (e.g., live preview SDK initializes at a different layer), AC-1, AC-8, and AC-13 may need adjustment.

after.description: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS — enable real-time preview of content changes made in the Contentstack CMS, so that editors see updated content on the live site without publishing.
after.title: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS

notes: Openspec provided zero ACs, so I created the full list from the story description and technical context. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1/AC-2 establish the core real-time update behavior with a 2-second SLA and targeted re-rendering. (2) AC-3 is a critical security/boundary criterion — Live Preview must be inert outside the CMS editor to avoid unnecessary connections and potential data leakage. (3) AC-5/AC-8 cover error resilience — connection drops and malformed data must not crash the UI. (4) AC-7 addresses accessibility for screen reader users during live content changes. (5) AC-10 prevents UI flickering from rapid updates. (6) AC-11 ensures no blank-flash on initial load. (7) AC-13 aligns with openspec's note that Contentstack APIs are unreachable at test time. (8) AC-15 prevents preview-mode side effects from leaking to production. CAVEAT: I could not read the four referenced files (hooks/useContent, ContentstackContext.ts, and two mock files), which may contain existing patterns, types, or constraints that would affect specificity. The ACs are written to be implementation-agnostic per the what-not-how rule.

after.title: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS

notes: Classified as novel — Live Preview is a new capability with no existing wiring. The useContent hook is the primary attachment point: 10+ components (NavigationBar, Footer, TopBar, ContentstackText, etc.) call it to fetch CMS content. Live Preview SDK integration must augment or wrap this hook to inject real-time content updates. ContentstackText is the simplest consumer for validation. Contentstack APIs are unreachable at test time, so VCs are scoped to our side of the boundary with explicit mock assumptions.

notes: Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria array with valuable context about useContent as the primary attachment point and ContentstackText as the simplest validation consumer. I created all ACs from scratch based on the story description, openspec's notes, and the listed file paths. File contents were unavailable, so ACs are inferred from story context alone — specific field-level behaviors in ContentstackText or useContent may need adjustment once implementation details are known. AC-1/2/3 cover core live preview behavior and multi-brand applicability. AC-4 covers the inactive-preview fallback path. AC-5/6 cover connection loss and reconnection edge cases. AC-7 covers SDK initialization failure. AC-8 covers rapid-update debouncing/convergence. AC-9 covers credential leakage prevention. AC-10 covers accessibility notification of dynamic content changes. AC-11 covers multi-component update consistency. AC-12 covers session teardown.
